scientific_readiness_exploratory_results.interpretation: Spike-valued I/O alone is insufficient to define a fully-spiking computational substrate when hidden continuous decoder/filter state may carry task-relevant memory. This is synthetic specification pressure only, not evidence for H9 or SparkBrain.

hypothesis_or_reduction_question: Can spike-valued I/O appear to preserve delayed behavior while memory is carried by hidden continuous decoder/filter state rather than non-sensory spike-mediated dynamics?
synthetic_or_dev_inputs_used: Generated A/B delayed-recall trials across silent gaps 1..20 only; no historical C07 rerun/tuning and no official/formal inputs.
implementation_or_experiment_performed: Implemented deterministic stateless, hidden analog-leaky, and toy recurrent-spike-latch comparators and recorded a fixed decay-grid sensitivity result on an explicitly exploratory branch.
observations: Hidden analog state reached 40/40 for decay 0.9, 0.95 and 0.99 while using zero non-sensory recurrent spikes.
At decay 0.8 it was 26/40 with full accuracy through gap 13; at 0.5 it was 8/40 through gap 4.
Toy recurrent spike latch was 40/40 and used mean 10.5 recurrent spikes per trial.
The only warranted lesson is that decoder/filter memory must be explicit in a future operational fully-spiking boundary.
what_would_falsify_or_reduce_it: A prospectively specified H9 successor that forbids task-relevant hidden continuous/algorithmic memory outside the declared spiking substrate, or proves such state task-irrelevant under a fixed inventory/ablation rule, would reduce this concern.
candidate_formal_question: After a fresh prospective definition, does a declared spike-mediated non-sensory substrate preserve fixed H9 behavioral invariants when task-relevant hidden continuous/algorithmic state outside that substrate is prohibited or explicitly resource-matched?
new_scientific_choices_required_before_f: allowed decoder/filter state and state-inventory rule
